audience: Students with basic programming knowledge learning assembly

progression.localImplementation: Native prose and public intermediate/final CLI checks; remote delivery and enforced instructor policies remain pending

title: Filter a PCM WAV file
prerequisites: Signed sixteen-bit PCM, interleaved frames and byte order
The earlier eight-tap Q15 FIR kernel and exact rounding
Nested calls, full-width saved registers and short file transfers
learningObjectives: Validate bounded RIFF chunks before publishing a descriptor
Keep PCM sample, frame and complete-file byte counts distinct
Retain per-channel input history across FIR blocks
Produce exact rounded and saturated sample codes
Write a canonical PCM container with unsigned capacity checks
Close acquired descriptors and preserve failed-validation outputs

inputDomain.extent: Exact complete file; format precedes one data chunk; bounded opaque chunks permitted; all trailing chunks validated

functionContract.memory: Exact disjoint selected intervals; byte pointers may be unaligned; descriptor aligned to eight bytes
functionContract.filter: Earlier exact eight-tap Q15, oldest-first coefficients, separate zero histories, N frames without a tail

steps.title: Distinguish the file from its description

quiz.prompt: What must the bound helper inspect?

choices.text: The description prefix addressed by a0.

hints.text: Treat a pointer as an address of a particular object, not as the value stored there.
At the call, a0 points to metadata: rate 16000, channels two and four frames. The eighty-two-byte source remains a separate object.

steps.title: Bring forward the tested FIR entry

quiz.prompt: What does the raw FIR return value four mean?

hints.text: Read the earlier kernel contract before assigning a meaning to v0.
The raw kernel returns four processed samples and zero clips. Its four output codes are 1500, 1500, 500 and 4596.

steps.title: Read the prefix at its declared widths

quiz.prompt: How wide is the frame-count field?

hints.text: Field width is part of the call contract even when the example value is small.
The three working values are 16000, two and four; no file or sample bytes have been accessed.

steps.title: Validate before multiplying

quiz.prompt: Why check the frame count as unsigned?

choices.text: The helper accepts all register bit patterns.
A top-bit-set count is outside the supported domain.

hints.text: Use the documented upper bound before deriving any byte count.
The worked prefix passes. A prefix with 65537 frames must fail with status one and zero count.

steps.title: Return the canonical file extent

quiz.prompt: What accounts for the difference between eighty-two and sixty bytes?

choices.text: The canonical result omits ancillary chunks.

hints.text: Count header bytes and PCM bytes separately before adding them.
The completed helper returns status zero and sixty bytes. A valid zero-frame prefix returns forty-four bytes.

steps.title: Reject impossible extents before reading pointers

quiz.prompt: Which check comes before reading the RIFF identifier?

hints.text: An input extent is not established merely because a pointer register has a value.
The worked count eighty-two reaches the parser frame. Early count failures clear v1 and do not access either caller object.

steps.title: Recognize the outer identifiers

quiz.prompt: Does WAVE alone establish sixteen-bit PCM?

choices.text: Yes; every WAV has the same sample encoding.
Yes, when the filename ends in wav.
No; the format chunk must establish that.

hints.text: Container identification and audio representation are separate checks.
Both identifiers match. Caller metadata is still unchanged.

steps.title: Check the exact outer extent

quiz.prompt: What does the RIFF size omit?

choices.text: The first eight bytes of the file.

hints.text: Compare the on-disk convention with the complete byte count received by the function.
The stored RIFF size is seventy-four, its complete extent is eighty-two, and the first chunk offset is twelve.

steps.title: Establish the next complete chunk span

quiz.prompt: Where does an odd payload length place the next chunk?

choices.text: Immediately after the last payload byte.

hints.text: Compute a bounded span before examining the chunk-specific fields.
The first chunk has payload length three, payload offset twenty and next chunk offset twenty-four.

steps.title: Dispatch recognized chunks and skip opaque ones

quiz.prompt: How should an unknown chunk be skipped?

hints.text: The next offset was established by the chunk-span check.
The first visit to parse_format describes the chunk at offset twenty-four, with a sixteen-byte payload at thirty-two.

steps.title: Observe the first skipped chunk

quiz.prompt: What determines whether the JUNK pad is valid?

choices.text: Its required presence within the chunk span.

hints.text: Count three payload bytes and then one pad from the JUNK payload start.
The current header starts at twenty-four. The nonzero pad was consumed by its position, not interpreted as audio or as a new identifier.

steps.title: Accept only the two format payload sizes

quiz.prompt: When should the format-seen flag be committed?

choices.text: After all supported format fields pass.
As soon as the identifier matches.

hints.text: An identified chunk can still contain an unsupported format.
The worked sixteen-byte format reaches parse_format_size. Its format-seen flag remains clear until all fields pass.

steps.title: Check the PCM encoding tag

quiz.prompt: Which value identifies the supported PCM encoding?

hints.text: The encoding tag occupies two bytes at the beginning of the format payload.
The format tag is one. Unsupported encoding tags take the format-failure route.

steps.title: Read and retain the channel count

quiz.prompt: How many sixteen-bit sample codes are in one stereo frame?

hints.text: Bits per sample describes each channel sample, not a complete frame.
The retained channel count is two, so each frame contains four PCM bytes.

steps.title: Read the sample rate as an unsigned field

quiz.prompt: What does the sample-rate field count for stereo audio?

choices.text: The sum of both channels' sample counts per second.

hints.text: Assemble the byte representation before interpreting the unit.
The bytes 80 3e 00 00 describe 16000 frames per second.

steps.title: Verify the redundant byte rate

quiz.prompt: Which expression gives the supported byte rate?

choices.text: Two times channels times sample rate.

hints.text: One frame holds two bytes for each channel.
The stored and computed rates are both 64000 bytes per second.

steps.title: Verify the frame byte width

quiz.prompt: Does block alignment make the caller's input pointer aligned?

choices.text: Yes; four-byte frames imply an aligned file base.
No; the byte-pointer contract still permits an unaligned address.
Yes; all file fields are halfword aligned in memory.

hints.text: Distinguish a format field from an address precondition.
The block alignment is four for stereo and would be two for mono.

steps.title: Require the supported sample width

quiz.prompt: Why reject a twenty-four-bit PCM description?

choices.text: The published processing interface supports sixteen-bit samples only.
RIFF can never contain that representation.

hints.text: Apply the local supported profile without making a claim about every WAV file.
The accepted field is sixteen. Neither output bytes nor caller metadata have changed.

steps.title: Check the optional empty extension

quiz.prompt: What changes when the empty extension adds two bytes?

choices.text: The later chunk and PCM offsets.

hints.text: The chunk length controls layout even when the added field is zero.
The eighteen-byte format has a zero extension count and an eighty-four-byte complete file. The later PCM offset will be fifty-eight.

steps.title: Commit the private format state

quiz.prompt: Where should the accepted rate live before the full walk succeeds?

hints.text: The input is read-only and the public descriptor is a success-only publication.
The private format flag is set and the next header begins at forty-eight for the ordinary trace. Caller metadata remains a sentinel.

steps.title: Require format before a unique data chunk

quiz.prompt: Why retain the original file base?

choices.text: Later chunks are still addressed relative to it.
The filter writes its history into the header.
The data offset is an absolute address.

hints.text: A file-relative offset becomes a pointer only when added to this particular buffer base.
The candidate PCM region begins at offset fifty-six and contains sixteen bytes.

steps.title: Convert a byte length to complete frames

quiz.prompt: What does a two-byte stereo data payload contain?

choices.text: An incomplete frame, which must fail.

hints.text: Test the remainder before using the quotient as an accepted frame count.
Sixteen PCM bytes divided by four bytes per frame gives four frames with no remainder.

steps.title: Continue beyond accepted sample bytes

quiz.prompt: Does accepting data finish the parser?

choices.text: Only if the frame count is nonzero.
No; all trailing chunks must also pass.
Yes; bytes after audio are ignored.

hints.text: The complete input count belongs to the container, not just the selected sample slice.
The next offset is seventy-two. The walker validates the final note chunk and then reaches the complete count eighty-two.

steps.title: Inspect the candidate before publication

quiz.prompt: Which object is still unchanged at parse_finish?

hints.text: Compare the descriptor sentinel with the candidate values in the parser frame.
Private state describes 16000 Hz, two channels, four frames, offset fifty-six and sixteen bytes; the caller descriptor is unchanged.

steps.title: Check completion and the overhead budget

quiz.prompt: Which bytes count toward outside-data overhead?

choices.text: Every complete-file byte outside the selected PCM payload.

hints.text: Include headers, format bytes and pads when subtracting the PCM payload length.
The trace has sixty-six overhead bytes, within the 4096-byte allowance.

steps.title: Publish the descriptor once

quiz.prompt: What is the parser's successful v1 unit?

hints.text: Use the parser contract even though the loader later returns a different count.
The published descriptor is (16000, two, four, fifty-six, sixteen), and the successful return count is four frames.

steps.title: Reject a malformed trailer without publication

quiz.prompt: Why adjust RIFF size in this malformed example?

choices.text: To reach the chunk-span failure rather than the outer-size failure.

hints.text: A useful negative test makes the intended invalid condition reachable.
The missing final pad produces status one and zero count; all descriptor bytes remain unchanged.

steps.title: Accept an empty stream with a real container

quiz.prompt: Is a zero-byte file a valid empty-audio input?

choices.text: Yes; zero frames require no description.
Only when its extension is wav.
No; empty audio still needs a valid container.

hints.text: Distinguish zero samples from zero supplied file bytes.
The fifty-eight-byte container passes with zero frames, PCM offset forty-six and PCM length zero.

steps.title: Validate the prefix through the shared helper

quiz.prompt: What must the filter do with a failed bound call?

choices.text: Propagate the failure before processing samples.
Treat v1 as a valid frame count.

hints.text: A nested success result has its own unit; it does not replace the outer interface.
The nested helper returns success and sixty bytes for the worked prefix; filter output is still untouched.

steps.title: Initialize per-call progress

quiz.prompt: Which input may be read for a valid zero-frame filter?

choices.text: One PCM sample to detect silence.

hints.text: Zero work is a specified access boundary, not just a loop that happens to stop.
The trace starts with four frames, two channels, channel index zero and zero clips.

steps.title: Start a channel with zero history

quiz.prompt: When must the illustrated wrapper clear history?

choices.text: Only once when the program first starts.
At the start of each channel of each invocation.

hints.text: The mathematical beginning condition applies independently to each channel.
The seven history samples are zero and the selected channel begins at frame zero.

steps.title: Choose a bounded group of new samples

quiz.prompt: How many halfwords does a full input window contain?

hints.text: Add the retained history length to the new-sample count.
The four-frame trace selects a block of four new samples for the current channel.

steps.title: Gather one channel from interleaved PCM

quiz.prompt: What is the byte stride between successive left samples in stereo?

hints.text: Advance by a complete interleaved frame while keeping the channel index fixed.
The first channel window contains seven zeros followed by 12000, zero, minus 8000 and 32767.

steps.title: Call the kernel with a chronological window

quiz.prompt: Which condition confirms completion of the kernel block?

choices.text: Its v0 equals WAV status zero.
Its v1 equals the byte length.
Its processed count equals the requested block count.

hints.text: Keep the earlier FIR result convention at the nested-call boundary.
The first left-channel call processes four outputs and returns zero clips. Its private outputs are 1500, 1500, 500 and 4596.

steps.title: Accumulate clipping events in a wide count

quiz.prompt: What is the maximum number of sample results in a supported stereo file?

hints.text: Each of two channels can contribute one clipped result per frame.
The averaging coefficients produce zero clips for this first block; the accumulated total remains zero.

steps.title: Scatter results back into interleaved order

quiz.prompt: Which output slots may the first channel pass change?

choices.text: Only the selected channel's sample slots.
Every halfword before the current frame.
The input history slots in source.

hints.text: Use an interleaved destination stride even though the kernel output is contiguous.
The left output slots contain 1500, 1500, 500 and 4596 while right slots retain their sentinel bytes.

steps.title: Locate the retained input suffix

quiz.prompt: Which buffer supplies the next history?

hints.text: Subtract seven samples from the combined window length, not from the new-sample count.
For a four-sample block, the retained suffix begins eight bytes into the window: three zeros followed by the four new input samples.

steps.title: Copy history safely within the window

quiz.prompt: Why is forward copying safe here?

choices.text: The destination begins below the overlapping source.
The two regions are always disjoint.

hints.text: Trace source and destination addresses for a one-sample block.
The new history is three zeros followed by 12000, zero, minus 8000 and 32767.

steps.title: Advance by the actual block length

quiz.prompt: What is the second block size for sixty-five frames?

hints.text: The block limit and the amount actually processed are different quantities.
The short trace reaches frame four and finishes its first channel. A sixty-five-frame input would next select a one-frame block.

steps.title: Finish one channel before starting the next

quiz.prompt: What must happen when starting the right channel?

choices.text: Keep the left channel's final history.
Reset its frame cursor and zero its own history.

hints.text: Each channel represents a separate causal input sequence.
After the second channel, channel index equals two and both interleaved outputs are complete.

steps.title: Return status and the total clip count

quiz.prompt: Why does the caller save clips before encoding?

choices.text: The saved registers cannot hold counts.
Encoding returns a byte count in the same result register.
Encoding needs clips as its sample rate.

hints.text: Result registers are shared storage across calls, but their units belong to each interface.
The completed trace filter returns zero clips and produces sixteen PCM bytes in interleaved order.

steps.title: Observe a block boundary and a zero-frame call

quiz.prompt: What distinguishes the block boundary from a new channel?

choices.text: Input history continues across blocks of the same channel.

hints.text: Use an exact state check for the boundary; listening cannot establish bit-for-bit continuity.
The sixty-five-frame result is continuous across the block split. The zero-frame call succeeds with zero clips and touches only its prefix and invocation frame.

steps.title: Validate the description before producing output

quiz.prompt: Does the encoder use the parser's stored PCM offset?

choices.text: Yes; it adds that offset to a0.
No; a0 already points directly to PCM.

hints.text: Follow the encoder argument contract rather than the origin of the prefix.
The trace encoder receives sixteen PCM bytes and a successful canonical bound of sixty bytes.

steps.title: Check capacity before the first write

quiz.prompt: How should a capacity with its top bit set compare with sixty?

choices.text: As a request for zero bytes.

hints.text: Capacity is supplied as an unsigned sixty-four-bit count.
A capacity of sixty passes for the trace; fifty-nine fails with unchanged destination and zero count.

steps.title: Write the outer canonical header

quiz.prompt: Which RIFF size belongs to a sixty-byte canonical file?

hints.text: Apply the same outer-size convention used by the parser.
The trace header begins RIFF, size fifty-two, WAVE. Only its first twelve bytes have been authored so far.

steps.title: Write the canonical format identity

quiz.prompt: How long is the canonical format payload?

choices.text: Eighteen bytes whenever the input used eighteen.

hints.text: The writer has one published output layout independent of the input chunk arrangement.
The format payload starts at twenty and declares PCM with two channels.

steps.title: Write consistent rate fields

quiz.prompt: Which rate changes when channel count doubles at a fixed sample rate?

hints.text: Count bytes in one frame before multiplying by frames per second.
The trace writes 16000 frames per second and 64000 bytes per second.

steps.title: Write the frame width and sample width

quiz.prompt: Which field remains sixteen when converting this description to mono?

hints.text: Keep the units next to each field as you lay out the bytes.
The stereo header contains block alignment four and sample width sixteen.

steps.title: Write the data header for the exact PCM extent

quiz.prompt: Where does canonical PCM begin?

hints.text: The new file layout is independent of the parsed input offset.
The trace declares sixteen payload bytes, beginning at offset forty-four.

steps.title: Copy sample bytes without changing their codes

quiz.prompt: Does canonical encoding filter the PCM a second time?

choices.text: Only if the source was stereo.
No; it copies the supplied PCM codes.

hints.text: The filter and container writer are separate operations with separate inputs.
The prepared encoder observation copies the sixteen worked raw PCM bytes after its header; bytes beyond the sixty-byte result remain sentinels.

steps.title: Return the complete encoded byte count

quiz.prompt: Which count should the saver receive from the encoder?

choices.text: The actual returned complete file count.

hints.text: A buffer's size and its current valid file extent are separate values.
The trace returns sixty complete file bytes; empty audio returns forty-four.

steps.title: Read the canonical output independently

quiz.prompt: Why use an independent reader?

choices.text: A WAV parser must always be external.
Two routines can agree on the same incorrect layout.

hints.text: Compare the public format fields and exact samples, not only a successful return.
The result has a forty-four-byte canonical header, four stereo frames and unchanged sample bytes; the next byte remains a5.

steps.title: Validate the caller buffer capacity first

quiz.prompt: Is a one-byte capacity rejected by the capacity precheck?

choices.text: Only if the path is empty.
No; later transfer or format checks decide its result.
Yes; every capacity must be at least forty-four.

hints.text: Apply the loader capacity contract separately from the parser minimum file length.
The ordinary capacity passes; zero and a top-bit-set value fail before pointer access.

steps.title: Acquire a descriptor and initialize progress

quiz.prompt: Which value should later reads use as their descriptor?

choices.text: The value actually returned by open.

hints.text: A resource handle is an acquired result, not a constant in the file format.
A successful open leaves a live descriptor and zero accepted bytes. The grading fixture may choose a descriptor other than three.

steps.title: Accumulate actual positive read progress

quiz.prompt: What follows a positive short read?

choices.text: Advance by the actual count and read again.

hints.text: Use the syscall result as progress; the request is only an upper bound.
With forced short reads, accepted bytes remain contiguous and the next request starts immediately after the actual prefix.

steps.title: Distinguish an exact fit from excess input

quiz.prompt: Where may the exact-fit probe write?

choices.text: One byte beyond the caller buffer.

hints.text: The probe distinguishes stream length without extending the caller buffer.
The exact-capacity trace has eighty-two accepted bytes and a zero-byte probe; it proceeds to load_eof.

steps.title: Close before parsing the complete file

quiz.prompt: What count does a successful load return?

choices.text: Frames returned by the nested parser.

hints.text: Convert the nested result convention only after checking its status.
The successful trace load returns eighty-two bytes and the parsed descriptor, with no live file descriptor.

steps.title: Validate the complete count before pointer use

quiz.prompt: What must the saver receive?

choices.text: The full allocation including its guard.
A complete supported stream and its exact count.

hints.text: Saving an existing complete container is a different call from encoding PCM.
The eighty-two-byte trace passes the early count checks.

steps.title: Parse before opening for truncation

quiz.prompt: Why validate before the output open?

choices.text: Opening in truncate mode can destroy an existing file.
The parser needs a writable file.

hints.text: Resource acquisition can change external state before any write call.
The trace validates privately. A malformed trailer returns format failure without opening or changing the old output.

steps.title: Acquire output only after validation

quiz.prompt: Is the readable guard part of the saved file?

choices.text: No; it lies outside the exact file extent.
Yes; every saved WAV ends with a guard byte.

hints.text: A syscall memory-access requirement does not alter the file format.
The permitted output is now open with zero bytes written; the guard remains outside the selected count.

steps.title: Advance writes by actual progress

quiz.prompt: How should zero progress be handled?

hints.text: The loop needs positive progress to approach its finite complete count.
Forced short writes form a contiguous file prefix. Requested counts and accepted counts can differ.

steps.title: Close and return the selected count

quiz.prompt: Does a later write failure restore an old truncated file?

choices.text: Only when the status is three.
No; the contract permits the accepted output prefix.

hints.text: Distinguish validation-before-open from rollback after external writes begin.
The trace save returns eighty-two bytes and leaves no live output descriptor.

steps.title: Connect load, filter, encode and save

quiz.prompt: Which address does the pipeline pass to filtering?

choices.text: Source base plus the accepted PCM offset.

hints.text: The input chunk layout and canonical output layout have different PCM offsets.
The input is eighty-two bytes, output sixty bytes, and clips zero. The filtered PCM codes are 1500, minus 1500, 1500, 500, 500, 500, 4596 and minus 3596.

steps.title: Run the two-second observation after exact checks

quiz.prompt: What can listening establish about exact Q15 arithmetic?

choices.text: It is a qualitative observation alongside exact checks.

hints.text: Keep exact numeric checks as the acceptance condition before the longer playback observation.
The input has 128056 bytes and the canonical result 128044 bytes, both describing two seconds at 16000 Hz with two channels.
